findings.description: The instance user_data embeds a static AWS access key ID and secret access key in plaintext. These are stored in the Terraform source/state and are readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute, and the keys must be treated as compromised.
The security group admits SSH (tcp/22) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote administration of the portal server to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-based attacks.
HTTP (tcp/80) is open to 0.0.0.0/0, permitting any internet host to reach the web server on the instance.
The egress rule permits all protocols to all destinations (0.0.0.0/0), providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the instance.
The EBS volume has no encrypted = true setting, so the portal server disk is stored unencrypted and the snapshot derived from it is likewise unencrypted.
The snapshot of the portal disk is created without encryption, exposing a copy of the instance's data at rest outside the protections of an encrypted volume.
The VPC flow log archive bucket defines no server-side encryption configuration, so flow log records are stored unencrypted.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so instances launched in this subnet automatically receive public addresses and are directly internet-reachable.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, automatically assigning routable public IP addresses to instances in this subnet and exposing them to the internet.
A 0.0.0.0/0 route is pointed at the internet gateway and associated with both subnets, making them public subnets with a direct path to and from the internet.
